title: Externalized Authorization

validation.research: Five primary sources verified. OpenID Foundation AuthZEN explicitly names externalized authorization and the PDP/PEP family. Final OASIS XACML3.0 Standard22January2013 defines the roles and section7.2.2 deny-biased obligation handling; candidate/working drafts were not used as the article authority. OPA documents policy decision/enforcement separation. AWS documents centralized, distributed and library-based PDP models. Versioned Envoy documentation establishes explicit failure_mode_allow behavior. No existing exact canonical article found. External authorization is an integration term; RBAC/ABAC/ReBAC are policy models, and Policy as Code concerns rule representation/governance. No unsupported alias invented; existing data-policy-as-code preserved and related.

example_limits: Sequential in-process two-module responsibility model, not a deployed policy service/security kernel or protocol implementation. Authenticated subject, report metadata, grants and callback are trusted preconditions. No real timeout timer, service/network authentication, cryptographic response proof, durable policy distribution, cache or concurrent check/use protection. A matching old permit can be replayed in the model after revocation, and a forged callback can manufacture a permit; negative scope tests explicitly demonstrate these missing freshness/authenticity guarantees. Direct calls to the trusted current engine do observe P2 revocation in two handlers. Real adapters must protect the decision path, bind actual operations/facts, interpret obligations, coordinate policy/data versions and cache lifetime, and guard all alternate access paths.
